applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Public engineering guidance on structural load paths; not a code-specific design module.

claims.text: A load path is the route by which actions are transferred through structural parts and connections to supports and foundations.

source_refs.locator: Continuous Load Path Provided with Connections from the Roof through the Wall to the Foundation

claims.text: Continuous load paths depend on connected chains of members and connections; discontinuities, openings, or missing connectors can interrupt gravity, uplift, or lateral transfer.
Fraia should ask for or infer load paths at the system level before treating local member forces as meaningful design actions.

limitations: Some public load-path sources are residential or hazard-focused; transfer concepts must be re-scoped for steel portal frames and other systems.
A verbal load path is not a substitute for resolved topology, connection assumptions, or analysis.

pages_used: Continuous Load Path Provided with Connections from the Roof through the Wall to the Foundation

summary: Fraia should reason about how gravity, uplift, lateral, and stability actions travel through connected structural objects before trusting local member or reaction results.
title: Load Paths
